concerns.text: The plan does not provide a power analysis or justify that the QM9 subset size will yield sufficient statistical power for the paired t‑test (SC‑002). It merely assumes “sufficient power for medium‑large effect sizes” without quantifying sample size or effect size expectations.

The paired t‑test assumes normality and independence of error differences, yet no diagnostic checks (e.g., Shapiro‑Wilk, QQ‑plot) are specified. If the error distribution deviates from normality, the test may be invalid.

Model capacity and hyper‑parameter tuning are not controlled across the GNNs and the Random Forest baseline. Without matching model complexity or a systematic hyper‑parameter search, performance differences could be confounded by unequal model expressiveness rather than the graph‑based representation.

The alignment‑score threshold (≥ 0.7) for attribution validation is arbitrary and lacks justification or a pre‑registered null‑distribution analysis. The plan mentions a null‑model baseline but does not describe how the threshold will be derived from it.

The proxy validation (SC‑006) relies on a Pearson correlation with only n = 20 kinetic data points and explicitly states no formal hypothesis test will be performed. This limits the ability to draw any inferential conclusion about the proxy’s validity.
